post.caption:
The siren's pitch never changes. Because the source is moving, each new pressure wave starts from slightly closer than the last, which bunches the waves ahead of it and stretches them behind. More waves per second arriving is exactly what a higher pitch is, so the pitch you hear belongs to the motion, not the siren. The same effect drives radar speed guns and weather radar, and applied to light it is how we measure the expanding universe.
